answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before it may attest work, with slashing for contradictory claims. Like a ship that may begin only one voyage at a time from a single jetty, one bond backs exactly one active identity, so spawning a thousand fakes means locking a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn their bond back with interest over time, while a velvet-smooth flood of fake attestations collapses: each contradiction forfeits the attacker's stake, turning mass fakery from nearly free into a losing, capital-hungry gamble.
